marks.english: Where Yixing marks are placed: base, lid, handle
marks.description: Ming (Shi Dabin era): carved regular-script signature on the base. Qing: seals stamped as well as carved; by the Jiaqing period the rule was inscription carved on the body, seals on base, lid and handle. Republic and later: base + lid + handle seals standard (e.g. Cheng Shouzhen: base inscription, 壽珍 lid, 真記 handle).
marks.what_it_is: From the Qing onward a fine Yixing pot often carries a base seal, a smaller seal inside the lid and a tiny seal under the handle; Ming pots were usually incised on the base.
marks.dating_value: A full three-seal set suggests 19th century or later; a single incised base signature suits the Ming but is easy to copy.

marks.dating_value: A form name, not a maker's mark; the type was mass-produced in the Cultural Revolution.

facts.claim: Shuiping pots have rim, spout tip and handle top flush when inverted; the Mengchen form came to be called shuiping.

sources.name: Victoria and Albert Museum, teapot FE.1B&C-1984 (Shao Jingnan)
sources.says: having a shui ping (water level): the mouthrim, the tip of the spout and the top of the handle are all flush

sources.name: 百度百科 Baidu Baike, entry「惠孟臣」 (read in a browser 2026-11-26)
sources.says: 其壶式被后世称为水平壶并广泛仿制

facts.claim: A 1850–1900 Mengchen-type pot has 水平 stamped inside the cover.

sources.name: Victoria and Albert Museum, teapot FE.9:1, 2-1990 (Mengchen mark, 1850–1900)
sources.says: 水平 … shuiping … Inside cover

facts.claim: During the Cultural Revolution the factory mass-produced shuiping pots.

sources.name: Wikipedia, 'Number One Yixing Factory' (cites Pan Chunfang, Yixing Pottery, 2004)
